story.titleZh: 克拉克、塞纳、安东内利——大满贯年龄纪录的演变

story.originalTitle: Clark, Senna, Antonelli – How the grand chelem age record has evolved
story.summaryEn: The age record for F1 grand chelems (pole position, leading every lap, winning, and setting the fastest lap) has been repeatedly broken. Juan Manuel Fangio became the first grand chelem winner at the 1950 Monaco Grand Prix at the age of 38 years, 10 months, and 27 days, and since then drivers like Jim Clark and Ayrton Senna have successively broken the record, while recently Andrea Kimi Antonelli may have broken it again.
detailZh: 克拉克、塞纳、安东内利——大满贯年龄纪录的演变
今年早些时候，基米·安东内利成为最年轻的大满贯（或大满贯）得主——这一纪录几乎只有F1最伟大的车手才曾保持过。
历史上第一个大满贯——从杆位领跑整场比赛并在获胜途中创造最快圈速——发生在F1世界锦标赛的第二场比赛中。
未来的五届世界冠军胡安·曼努埃尔·方吉奥在排位赛中最快，领先2.6秒。这位38岁的阿根廷人在Tabac弯角通过后，港口涌来的波浪浸湿了赛道，导致大部分车手出局，包括从发车区前五名起步的其他四位车手。
“我非常幸运，”方吉奥告诉Autosport，否认了他可能拥有“第六感”的说法。“1936年发生过类似事件，我碰巧在比赛前一天在汽车俱乐部看到了一张照片。
“当我从减速弯出来时，我意识到观众有些不同。我领先，但他们没有看我。他们正沿着道路向下看。我看到的是他们的后脑勺，而不是他们的脸。Tabac那里有比领先者更有趣的事情。
“然后我想起了那张照片，并尽可能用力刹车。非常接近。”
方吉奥随后套圈了所有对手。这绝不是他最精彩的驾驶，但它仍然创造了历史。
直到阿尔贝托·阿斯卡里和法拉利在1952年和1953年赛季（按F2规则运行）占据主导地位，才出现了其他大满贯，他们的霸权在短短14场比赛中产生了5个大满贯。
其中第一个是1952年在鲁昂举行的首届法国大奖赛。阿斯卡里以2分14.8秒跑完5.1公里的赛道，分别比法拉利队友朱塞佩·法里纳和皮耶罗·塔鲁菲快1.4秒和2.3秒。
阿斯卡里在没有进站的情况下完成了388公里的比赛，甚至一场阵雨也无法阻挡他的统治。他以1分10.7秒的优势领先法里纳夺冠，塔鲁菲落后一圈，其他人更远。
下一位加入大满贯行列的车手是迈克·霍索恩——第一位在20多岁时实现这一成就的车手。
这位长期效力法拉利的车手在过去几年中一直是前三名的常客——他在1952年英国大奖赛上以23岁的年龄驾驶私人参赛的库珀成为F1历史上最年轻的领奖台完赛者。但1958年法国大奖赛只是他的第三场——也是最后一场——胜利。
作为那个赛季迄今为止唯一每场比赛都得分的车手，霍索恩在积分榜上落后于两届冠军斯特林·莫斯，但他在兰斯获得杆位，领先法拉利队友兼对手路易吉·穆索0.7秒，莫斯落后2秒排在第六。
穆索在早期追赶霍索恩，但在第10圈冲出赛道。三周前在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道经历了一场严重撞车后幸存，这位33岁的意大利人被抛出翻滚的法拉利，几小时后去世。
霍索恩随后在无人挑战的情况下获胜，领先莫斯24.6秒，这竟成了他最后一场F1胜利。由于莫斯的公平竞赛——后者在霍索恩面临葡萄牙大奖赛取消资格时为他辩护——霍索恩以微弱优势加冕世界冠军。
霍索恩在赢得冠军后宣布退役，仅三个月后遭遇致命道路事故。他年仅29岁。
回到1962年，莲花车队推出了非常成功的莲花25——一款14次大奖赛冠军得主——吉姆·克拉克证明了他能充分发挥其潜力。
年仅26岁的克拉克在那一年成为真正的冠军争夺者，但机械问题使他在前四轮中的三轮退出竞争，而他在斯帕-弗朗科尔尚赛道从第12位发车赢得首胜，因此大满贯无望。
然而在安特里，克拉克获得了职业生涯第三个杆位（最终创纪录的33个），领先约翰·苏尔特斯0.6秒，并全程领跑这位同胞的Bowmaker参赛的Lola。他缓慢但轻松地拉开差距，以49.2秒获胜。
克拉克可能只获得过两个世界冠军，因为可靠性问题在62、64和67年让他付出巨大代价，但他在1968年4月在霍根海姆的一场F2比赛中不幸去世前，实现了8个大满贯——至今仍是纪录。
在接下来的23年里，不少于10位车手获得过大满贯，但只有艾尔顿·塞纳的出现提供了打破“最年轻”纪录的机会。
塞纳在托尔曼令人印象深刻的新秀赛季后，加入莲花车队，这只是他F1的第二个赛季。在雅卡雷帕瓜，他排位第四，一直跑到第三，直到发生电气故障，而他在埃斯托里尔的表现确实令人印象深刻。
这位25岁的巴西人在干燥条件下获得压倒性杆位，这是他创纪录的65个杆位中的第一个，比迈凯伦的阿兰·普罗斯特快0.413秒。比赛中大雨肆虐，26名参赛者中只有9人在方格旗前被归类。
塞纳在第一圈后领先队友埃利奥·德·安吉利斯2.65秒，第10圈领先12.9秒，并继续拉开差距，最终领先法拉利的米凯莱·阿尔博雷托63秒获胜。他与莲花车队经理彼得·沃尔分享的庆祝成为F1民间传说。
“赛车到处打滑——很难控制住它，”塞纳赛后评论道。“你经常看到赛车仅仅因为缺乏抓地力和动力过大而到处打滑。我对赛车唯一的问题是刹车，但在这种条件下你预料到了。
“一旦你接近某人，你什么都看不见。人们认为我没有犯错，但事实并非如此——我不知道我冲出赛道多少次！有一次我四个轮子都在草地上，完全失控，赛车又回到了赛道上。
“每个人都说‘惊人的赛车控制’，但那只是运气。”
多年后，当有人提出他1993年多宁顿大师级表现是他最伟大的驾驶时，塞纳不同意：“不可能！我有牵引力控制。
“好吧，我在多宁顿没有犯任何真正的错误，但赛车驾驶起来容易得多。这是一场不错的胜利，当然，但与1985年埃斯托里尔相比，真的不算什么！”
塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔，红牛赛车小红牛7雷诺
与这份名单上的其他所有车手不同，塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔在获得首个大满贯时已经是世界冠军。
这位红牛神童曾多次接近，包括2009年英国大奖赛——他提前三圈进站，暂时将领先让给了队友马克·韦伯——以及2011年欧洲大奖赛，他比菲利佩·马萨早一圈换胎，因此短暂地让出了第一位置。
还有2009年日本大奖赛，他从杆位领跑到胜利——但韦伯以0.003秒的优势抢走了最快圈速。
尽管如此，维特尔终于在F1首次访问印度时将所有要素整合在一起。他在排位赛中以0.296秒的优势力压刘易斯·汉密尔顿，以0.271秒的优势超过韦伯获得最快圈速，并在前10圈领先简森·巴顿4.8秒，在通往8.4秒胜利的路上大致保持了这个差距。
但红牛对维特尔的最快圈速英雄主义并不兴奋。至于他的车手是否请求允许完成大满贯，车队老板克里斯蒂安·霍纳说：“当然没有，因为他知道我们不喜欢这样。
“我们已经尽力管理它，我们调低了所有引擎模式，关闭了KERS，除了在赛道上放一头牛，我们无能为力。
“归根结底，我们完全信任他。我相信他还有余量，他的主要目标是赢得比赛。他知道最快圈速没有积分，但他喜欢那些小统计数据来完成一个完美的周末。”
那天，维特尔还打破了奈杰尔·曼塞尔单赛季领跑圈数纪录——2011赛季结束时为739圈，而这位英国偶像在1992年为694圈，尽管曼塞尔的命中率更高，而马克斯·维斯塔潘在2023年彻底打破了这一纪录。
维斯塔潘在第128次尝试时成为F1最年轻的大满贯得主，这有点奇怪——这与方吉奥、阿斯卡里和霍索恩参加的比赛总数一样多——但这只是反映了他17岁首次参加大奖赛，并且在2021年之前从未真正拥有最快赛车的事实。
detailEn: Clark, Senna, Antonelli – How the grand chelem age record has evolved
Earlier this year, Kimi Antonelli became the youngest driver to score a grand chelem (or grand slam) – a record that (almost) only the greatest of F1 drivers have ever held
The first-ever grand chelem – leading the whole race from pole position and setting the fastest lap on your way to victory – occurred in just the second race of the Formula 1 world championship.

Future five-time title winner Juan Manuel Fangio was fastest by 2.6s in qualifying. The 38-year-old Argentine made it past Tabac corner right before a wave from the harbour soaked the track, which wiped out most of the field, including the other four drivers who started from the top five.

“I was very lucky,” Fangio told Autosport, denying suggestions that he might have a ‘sixth sense’. “There had been a similar incident in 1936 and I happened to see a photograph of it at the Automobile Club the day before the race.

“As I came out of the chicane, I was aware that there was something different with the crowd. I was leading, but they were not watching me. They were looking down the road. Instead of seeing their faces, I was seeing the backs of their heads. Something at Tabac was more interesting than the leader.
“And then I remembered that photograph and braked as hard as I could. It was very close.”
Fangio went on to lap all of his rivals. This wasn’t his most fantastic drive by any means, but it still made history.
No other grand chelem was achieved until Alberto Ascari and Ferrari dominated the 1952 and 1953 seasons, run to Formula 2 regulations, with their supremacy yielding five grand slams in just 14 races.

The first one of those was the inaugural Rouen-based French Grand Prix, in 1952. Ascari lapped the 5.1km track in 2m14.8s, outpacing Ferrari team-mates Giuseppe Farina and Piero Taruffi by 1.4s and 2.3s respectively.

Ascari completed the 388km race with no pitstops, and even a rain shower couldn’t thwart his dominance. He took the chequered flag 1m10.7s ahead of Farina, with Taruffi a lap down and everyone else further adrift.
The next driver to join the grand chelem ranks was Mike Hawthorn – the first one to do so in his 20s.

The longtime Ferrari racer had been a consistent top-three achiever over the previous years – he became F1’s youngest-ever podium finisher at just 23 in the 1952 British Grand Prix with a privately-entered Cooper. But the 1958 French GP marked just his third – and last – victory.

The only driver to have scored points in every race so far that season, Hawthorn was led by two-time winner Stirling Moss in the standings, but he took pole position at Reims, leading Ferrari team-mate and rival Luigi Musso by seven tenths, with Moss two seconds adrift in sixth.

Musso chased Hawthorn early on but went off the track on lap 10. Three weeks on from surviving a hefty crash at Spa-Francorchamps, the 33-year-old Italian was thrown out of his somersaulting Ferrari and died a few hours later.

Hawthorn went on to win unchallenged, 24.6s ahead of Moss, in what turned out to be his final F1 victory. He was narrowly crowned the world champion, courtesy of Moss’s fair-play, as the latter stood up for Hawthorn when he was facing disqualification from the Portuguese GP.
Hawthorn announced his retirement after winning the title and suffered a fatal road accident just three months later. He was 29 years old.
Back in 1962, Team Lotus introduced its highly successful Lotus 25 – a 14-time grand prix winner – and Jim Clark proved he could get the most of it.

Aged just 26, Clark became a bona fide title contender that year, but mechanical problems took him out of contention in three of the first four rounds, while he took his maiden win at Spa-Francorchamps – from 12th on the grid, so a grand chelem wasn’t on the cards.

At Aintree however, Clark claimed his third career pole of what would be a record 33, outpacing John Surtees by 0.6s, and led his compatriot’s Bowmaker-entered Lola throughout the race. He slowly but comfortably pulled away and won by 49.2s.

Clark may have clinched just two world titles, as unreliability cost him dear in ’62, ’64 and ’67, but he achieved eight grands chelems – still a record to this day – before his untimely death in an F2 race at Hockenheim in April 1968.
No fewer than 10 drivers scored grands chelems over the next 23 years, but only Ayrton Senna’s emergence provided an opportunity to beat the ‘youngest’ record.

Senna joined Lotus for what was just his sophomore F1 season after an impressive rookie campaign with Toleman. At Jacarepagua, he qualified fourth and ran third until an electrical failure occurred, and his Estoril performance was genuinely impressive.

The 25-year-old Brazilian took a dominant pole position in dry conditions, his first of a record 65, 0.413s faster than McLaren’s Alain Prost. Rain wreaked havoc in the race, with only nine of the 26 runners classified under the chequered flag.

Senna was 2.65s clear of team-mate Elio de Angelis after lap one, 12.9s ahead on lap 10, and kept pulling away to triumph 63 seconds ahead of Ferrari’s Michele Alboreto. The celebration he shared with Lotus team manager Peter Warr is etched into F1 folklore.

“The car was sliding everywhere – it was very hard to keep [it] under control,” Senna commented afterwards. “You often saw cars sliding about all over the place purely through lack of grip and too much power. The only problem [I had] with the car was the brakes, but under these conditions you expect that.

“Once you were close to someone, you could not see anything. People think I made no mistakes, but that’s not true – I’ve no idea how many times I went off! Once I had all four wheels on the grass, totally out of control, and the car came back on the circuit.
“Everyone said ‘Fantastic car control’ but it was just luck.”
And when, years later, it was suggested that his 1993 Donington masterclass was his greatest drive, Senna disagreed: “No way! I had traction control.
“OK, I didn’t make any real mistakes [at Donington], but the car was so much more easier to drive. It was a good win, sure, but compared with Estoril ’85 it was nothing, really!”
Sebastian Vettel, Red Bull Racing RB7 Renault
Unlike every other driver on this list, Sebastian Vettel was already a world champion when he clinched his maiden grand chelem.

The Red Bull prodigy had come close several times, including the 2009 British GP – where he temporarily lost the lead to team-mate Mark Webber as he pitted three laps earlier – and the 2011 European GP, where he changed tyres one lap before Felipe Massa and therefore conceded first place ever so briefly.
There was also the 2009 Japanese GP, which he led from pole to victory – but Webber snatched the fastest lap away by 0.003s.

Still, Vettel finally put it all together on F1’s inaugural visit to India. He topped qualifying by a healthy 0.296s over Lewis Hamilton, outpaced Webber by 0.271s for the fastest lap, and pulled away from Jenson Button by 4.8s in the first 10 laps, roughly maintaining that gap on his way to an 8.4s victory.

But Red Bull wasn’t thrilled with Vettel’s fastest-lap heroics. As to whether his driver had asked for permission to complete the grand chelem, team boss Christian Horner said: “Of course not because he knows we don't like it.
“We had done our best to manage it, we had turned all the engine modes down, KERS off, and short of putting a cow on the circuit there was not a lot else we could do.

“At the end of the day we have complete trust in him. I am sure he still had the margin in there, and the main aim for him is to win the race. He knows there are no points for fastest laps, but he likes those little statistics to complete a perfect weekend.”

That day, Vettel also broke Nigel Mansell’s record for most laps led in a season – 739 by the end of the 2011 season to the British icon’s 694 in 1992, though Mansell’s hit rate was higher and Max Verstappen obliterated that one in 2023.

It can be somewhat quaint that Verstappen became F1’s youngest grand chelem scorer at the 128th time of asking – as many races as the combined Fangio, Ascari and Hawthorn have competed in – but that’s just a reflection of the fact he made his grand prix debut at 17 and never really had the fastest car before 2021.

relatedItems.summaryEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed why he was on average more than 1.7 seconds per lap slower than his Cadillac team-mate Sergio Perez at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race-day intra-team deficit of the 2026 season so far.
detailZh: 瓦尔特里·博塔斯透露了上一站巴库比赛中，他相比凯迪拉克F1队友塞尔吉奥·佩雷兹速度严重不足的一些原因。
在阿塞拜疆大奖赛上，博塔斯平均每圈比佩雷兹慢超过1.7秒之多，这是2026赛季迄今正赛中最大的队内差距。甚至他的最快单圈也比佩雷兹慢1.489秒。
博塔斯在最后一圈撞上护墙，因为他在驶过1号弯逃生通道后，赛车的能量输出模式“有点混乱”，而由于多跑了距离，他在进入15号弯左弯时后刹车失效，车头撞上了护墙。
但更令人担忧的是此前惊人的速度差距，在博塔斯撞车之前，佩雷兹几乎已经套了他一圈。
“我理解从外面看起来情况很糟糕，坐在车里感觉也很糟糕，”博塔斯周四在马来西亚说。
“当时根本没办法跟上大部队。我在比赛中尝试了所有办法，也得到了很多关于我在哪里损失时间的反馈。很大一部分是在直道上，但也有相当大的一部分是在整圈的弯道中损失掉的。
“所以我一直在坚持推进直到最后，这也是为什么我在最后一圈进一号弯时锁死了轮胎。
“不过是的，关键问题是在练习中我们就已经看到我的速度不够。我无法像佩雷兹那样以同样的速度过弯，所以我们在排位赛前做了很多改动，包括一些减震器和底板，结果感觉确实好多了。
“但在正赛中，行驶品质又明显衰减了很多……我们这次改动了很多东西，所以我觉得问题在于减震器随温度衰减，还有底板……我们在某些地方仍然缺少一些压力测量点，所以对于气动部件，我还拿不到过去习惯获得的完整信息。
“通过数据你马上就能看出性能是提升还是下降，但现在底板有一些区域我们完全看不见。不过就我个人的感觉而言，更多问题出在行驶品质上——再加上动力转向整个周末都在不断衰减。所以我在整场比赛中真的很难去感受赛车。
“这些因素叠加在一起。而且动力单元的差距可能比我们预想的要大，至少从数据上看是这样。
“理论上我们有一个数字，但那是新引擎对全新引擎，也就是新规格对旧规格的对比。所以，我想就是这些因素叠加的结果。我当时确实相当慢。”
动力单元方面的差异指的是佩雷兹在巴库已经用上了升级版 ADUO 2 法拉利引擎，而博塔斯还没有。
此前这被描述为“细微差别”，但正如博塔斯所说，这次升级的效果可能比最初想象的更大。
博塔斯表示，他的 ADUO 2 引擎能否及时送到、让他能在雪邦赛道使用，可能性是“五五开”；如果赶不上，他就得等到下周的新加坡大奖赛。
他的队友佩雷兹本周末不会使用这套引擎，而是换用自己引擎池中的另一套动力单元，以便把升级版留到更能发挥作用的比赛周末再使用。
佩雷斯解释说：“我们做出了一个我们认为胜算最大的决定。”
“这就是为什么我们会在这里承受一些损失。但我们希望这会有所回报。”
“我们对这个周末并不太乐观。所以我们决定把它省下来。”
正如佩雷斯所暗示的，凯迪拉克的车手们已经为艰难的周末做好了准备，因为雪邦赛道带来了两个凯迪拉克尤其难以应对的挑战：轮胎过热和高速弯角。
正如佩雷兹所解释的，凯迪拉克目前“赛车的下压力严重不足，而且阻力很大”。
“在巴库，我基本上整场比赛都保持在超车模式上，所以才能跟住其他车手，”佩雷兹说。
“但当我超过他们之后，我就只能像个乘客一样，因为我没有直道速度。所以我们有两大问题：下压力不足和很大的阻力。”
“但我们一直都知道，第一年会很艰难。”
detailEn: Valtteri Bottas has revealed some of the reasons behind his woeful lack of pace compared to Cadillac Formula 1 team-mate Sergio Perez last time out in Baku.

Bottas was on average over a whopping 1.7 seconds slower than Perez per lap at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, the largest race day intra-team deficit of 2026 so far. Even his single fastest lap was 1.489s slower than Perez.

Bottas ended up in the wall on the final lap as his car’s deployment pattern “got a bit confused” because he went down the Turn 1 escape road, then because of the extra distance travelled his rear brakes didn’t work going into the Turn 15 left-hander, where he nosed into the barriers.
But what was more worrying was the alarming lack of pace before then, with Perez close to lapping Bottas before the latter's crash.
“I understand it looked pretty bad from the outside and felt pretty bad in the car as well,” Bottas said on Thursday in Malaysia.

“There was just no way to keep up with the pack. I tried everything during the race, and got lots of feedback on where I am losing the time. A lot of it was on the straights, but also a big chunk was just all around the lap in the corners.
“That's why I just kept pushing until the end and that's why I had to lock up on the last lap into Turn 1.

“But yeah, the main thing was we saw already in practice that I was lacking pace. I couldn't carry the same speed through the corners as Checo, so we changed a lot for the qualifying, including some dampers and the floor, and it actually felt a lot better.

“But then the ride again during the race degraded quite a lot... Again, we've changed a lot of things, so I think it's something to do with dampers degging with heat, the floor... We are still lacking a bit of pressure tappings here and there, so we still don't have the full information on aero parts that I'm used to from the past.

“You can immediately see if you're down or up, but now there are some bits of the floor where we are blind. But for me, feeling-wise, it was more the ride - that, in combination with the power steering that was degging throughout the weekend. So I was really then also struggling to feel the car throughout the race.
“So those things combined. And then the [power unit] difference was probably bigger than we thought, at least from the data.
“We've got a number in theory, but that's new engine versus new one, of the new and old spec. So yeah, I think those combined. I was pretty slow.”
The power unit difference is in reference to Perez having the upgraded ADUO 2 Ferrari engine in Baku while Bottas doesn’t yet have it.
This was previously described as a “small difference”, but as Bottas says the upgrade may be more powerful than first thought.
Bottas says it’s “50/50” if his ADUO 2 engine arrives in time for him to run it at Sepang; if not, he’ll have to wait until next week in Singapore.
Team-mate Perez won’t be running it this weekend, swapping to a different power unit in his pool in order to save it for a weekend when it will be more beneficial.
“We took a decision where we feel we got the best shot at it,” Perez explained.
“That's why we're taking a bit of a hit here. But we hope that it will pay us back.
“We are not too optimistic about this weekend. So we decided to save it.”
As Perez alluded, the Cadillac drivers are braced for a difficult weekend because Sepang poses two challenges the Cadillac struggles with in particular: tyre overheating and high-speed corners.
As Perez explains, the Cadillac has “a massive lack of load in the car and a lot of drag” right now.
“In Baku, I basically stayed on the overtake mode for the entire race and therefore I was able to stay with the others,” Perez said.
“But when I overtook them, I was just a passenger because I had no straightline speed. So we have two big issues: load and a lot of drag.
“But we always knew this first year was going to be tricky.”

relatedItems.originalTitle: Toyota denies 2027 WEC deal with Esteban Ocon
relatedItems.summaryEn: Toyota has denied it will sign Esteban Ocon for the World Endurance Championship in 2027, saying it does not want to jeopardise the harmony within its driver lineups. This follows Haas officially announcing it will end its partnership with the 30-year-old Frenchman at the conclusion of the 2026 season.
detailZh: 丰田否认2027年与奥孔达成WEC协议
这家日本制造商不想破坏其车手阵容内部的和谐
奥孔在F1的选择正逐渐减少，而丰田不会在世界耐力锦标赛（WEC）为他提供席位。
在哈斯车队本周官宣将在2026赛季结束后结束与这位30岁法国车手的合作之后，媒体上关于奥孔职业生涯下一步去向的猜测甚嚣尘上。
随着阿斯顿·马丁确认将继续留用阿隆索和斯特罗尔，凯迪拉克实际上成为奥孔在一级方程式中最后一个现实的选择。
这也正是他还与转投世界耐力锦标赛的可能性联系在一起的原因——可能加盟丰田。但丰田顾问亚历山大·伍尔茨现已向Motorsport.com姊妹刊物Formel1.de的YouTube频道明确表示：“这些传闻毫无根据。”
伍尔茨表示，丰田在勒芒及其世界耐力锦标赛项目上通常会做“相当长远的”规划，目前不打算对现有的六人车手阵容做出任何调整。
“因为当你把三个强势个性放进同一辆赛车时，他们需要时间去彼此接受，去找到正确的调校和正确的合作方式，并达到这样一个阶段：他们不再在内部互相竞争，而是真正激发出彼此的最佳状态。这是一个非常重要的区别，”这位奥地利人解释道。
#8 丰田Gazoo Racing 丰田TR010：塞巴斯蒂安·布耶米、布伦登·哈特利、平川亮
"这是丰田的优势之一：我们拥有这样的车队架构和车队文化，而这种东西不可能一夜之间改变。
"首先，我们签的是长期合同。其次，你不可能随便从外面引进一名车手，直接把他塞进车手阵容里。那样做恰恰有可能破坏我们自2012年以来一直建立并悉心呵护的文化。维护这种文化是我作为顾问、作为与车手密切合作的人的主要职责之一。
他还补充道："但不管你怎么看，这些合同都是长期的，而且我们明年的车手阵容已经百分之百满了。"
丰田目前参加世界耐力锦标赛（WEC），一台车由迈克·康威、尼克·德弗里斯和小林可梦伟驾驶，另一台车由塞巴斯蒂安·布埃米、布伦登·哈特利和平川亮驾驶。这家日本厂商刚刚在家乡富士赛道赢得胜利，在惊心动魄的尾声中，本地英雄平川亮完成了决定胜负的最后一段驾驶。
detailEn: Toyota denies 2027 WEC deal with Esteban Ocon
The Japanese manufacturer doesn't want to jeopardise the harmony within its driver lineups
Esteban Ocon’s Formula 1 options are gradually running out, and Toyota will not provide one in the WEC.

After Haas officially announced this week that it will end its partnership with the 30-year-old Frenchman at the conclusion of the 2026 season, media speculation has been rife over where Ocon’s career might take him next.
With Aston Martin having confirmed that it will continue with Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll, Cadillac effectively remains Ocon's last realistic option in Formula 1.

That is why he has also been linked with a possible switch to the World Endurance Championship – potentially with Toyota. But Toyota advisor Alexander Wurz has now made it clear to Motorsport.com sister publication Formel1.de’s YouTube channel: "There's nothing to these rumours."
Wurz said that Toyota generally plans "relatively far ahead" when it comes to Le Mans and its WEC programme, and that no changes to its current six-driver line-up are planned.

"Because when you put three alpha personalities in one car, it takes time for them to accept each other, to find the right set-up and the right way of working together, and to reach a point where they don't compete against each other internally but actually bring out the best in one another. That's a very important distinction," the Austrian explained.
#8 Toyota Gazoo Racing Toyota TR010: Sebastien Buemi, Brendon Hartley, Ryo Hirakawa
"That's one of Toyota's strengths: we have this team structure and this team culture, and you can't simply change that overnight.

"First of all, we have long-term contracts. And secondly, you can't just bring in another driver from the outside and slot him into the line-up. That would risk disrupting exactly the culture we've been building and nurturing since 2012. Maintaining that culture is one of my main responsibilities as an advisor and someone who works closely with the drivers.
He added: "But whichever way you look at it, the contracts are long-term and our line-up for next year is 100% full."

Toyota currently competes in the WEC with Mike Conway, Nyck de Vries and Kamui Kobayashi in one car, and Sebastien Buemi, Brendon Hartley and Ryo Hirakawa in the other. The Japanese manufacturer has just won its home race at Fuji, following a thrilling finish with local hero Hirakawa at the wheel for the decisive stint.
